_README: The defect corpus: deliberate breaks in the merge gate's own code, each run
against every rung of the gate's tests, to show which rung notices. Run by
`scripts/ci/mutation_sweep.py --rung-report`. An escape is a finding, not a
failure: it exits 0, and on main it means a test is owed, filed as an issue.
This is not `config/mutation_gate.json`, whose cases must all be caught.
`why` is written before running the case. `aim` is the rung that should catch
it. An anchor that stops matching fails `--check-anchors` on the PR that moved
it: update the case in that change.

cases.label: critical lane blocks on three P2s instead of two
cases.why: the lane table decides how many P2s block a critical change. Raising it lets a change to the gate itself merge past findings that should stop it.

cases.label: a Codex P1 on ordinary code no longer stops a merge
cases.why: the always-fix floor is what stops a lone P1 on ordinary code, which scores 1.0 against a threshold of 2.0. Without it that P1 passes the inline check with only a note.

cases.label: an unrecognised CI conclusion is ignored
cases.why: a conclusion GitHub adds later must read red. Ignoring it lets a run with that check merge on its sibling jobs' green.
cases.anchor:
red.append(name)
        elif status is not None or state in _CI_PENDING_STATES:
cases.replacement:
pass
        elif status is not None or state in _CI_PENDING_STATES:

cases.label: an abbreviated Codex id counts without resolving to the head
cases.why: a clean signal naming a prefix must resolve uniquely to this head across the repository. Otherwise a review of an older commit that shares the prefix reads as a review of this one.

cases.label: `# review-override` also waives red CI
cases.why: each override waives one named gate, because a waiver of findings is not a waiver of a red test run. A sigil that reaches a sibling lets a conscious yes on one thing merge past another.

cases.label: the leaks review is no longer required of anyone
cases.why: the leaks marker stops an install's private data reaching the public repo. Dropping the requirement for everyone removes that check from every owner PR that has not been reviewed.
cases.anchor: missing = [k for k in required if k not in kinds_here]
cases.replacement: missing = [k for k in required if k not in kinds_here and k != "leaks"]

cases.label: every inline finding counts as answered by a maintainer
cases.why: a maintainer's reply is what clears an inline finding, so treating an unanswered one as replied clears them all without anyone reading them.
cases.anchor:
c.get("reply_to")
        for c in raw
        if c.get("reply_to") and c.get("assoc") in _MAINTAINER_ASSOCIATIONS

cases.label: the inline findings read takes a comment's review id for the comment it replies to
cases.why: A REST review comment carries `in_reply_to_id`, absent on a top-level finding, and `pull_request_review_id`, present on every comment. Reading the second as the first makes every finding look like a reply, replies are never scored, and a Codex P1 merges. The other rungs feed this read its output after the jq filter, so only a rung that replays GitHub's raw answer through the filter can see it.
